Let \(F(x)=x-2\sin x\cos x+\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x\)

Using \(2\sin x\cos x=\sin 2x\)

we get \(F(x)=x-\sin 2x+\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x\)

Differentiating, \(F'(x)=1-2\cos 2x+\cos 3x\)

Let \(c=\cos x\).

Using \(\cos 2x=2c^2-1\) and \(\cos 3x=4c^3-3c\),

Therefore, \(x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) or \(x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\)

positive on \(\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\),

and negative on \(\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6},\pi\right)\)

Hence \(x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\) gives a local maximum

At the endpoints, \(F(0)=0\) and \(F(\pi)=\pi\)

At \(x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\),

\(F\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}-\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{3}+\dfrac{1}{3}\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\)

Therefore, \(F\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{5\pi+2+3\sqrt{3}}{6}\)

This value is greater than both endpoint values.
